question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023, which came into force on 1 July 2024, the provision defining rape is found in:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Section 375 is from the Indian Penal Code 1860, which was repealed by BNS 2023. BNS 2023 renumbered all provisions — the rape definition moved to Section 63.

Correct. BNS 2023 Section 63 replaces IPC Section 375 and defines rape by reference to seven circumstances (without consent, against will, under fear/fraud/intoxication, with a woman below 18 years, when she is of unsound mind, etc.). All medicolegal reports from 1 July 2024 onwards must cite BNS Section 63.
BNSS 2023 Section 397 is a procedural provision governing the examination of the accused in sexual offences — it is not the substantive rape definition.

POCSO Section 4 prescribes punishment for penetrative sexual assault on a child. POCSO is a separate legislation specifically for children under 18 years and does not define rape for the general population.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: IPC was replaced by BNS 2023 on 1 July 2024. Rape definition moved from IPC Section 375 to BNS Section 63. All MLCs from that date must cite the new provision.

Correct. BNS Section 63 is the operative provision from 1 July 2024. Every medicolegal opinion on rape cases must cite this section — citing the repealed IPC Section 375 in a report is a professional and legal error.
